The Story

Distributor. Founder. Operator.

Three chapters, one thread. I learn how a business makes money, I build the system that makes it repeatable, and I stay accountable for the number.

Act One

Learning the channel at scale

Tech Data / TD SYNNEX

As a Microsoft Cloud Account Executive and Channel Sales Leader, I learned the channel from the inside, working with leading vendors and hundreds of partners.

  • Carried a $44M annual channel goal
  • Grew partner led gross profit by more than $2M
  • Built repeatable partner practices around joint cloud offerings
  • Circle of Excellence, 2013 to 2015, and the top North American cloud and hybrid producer in 2015
Act Two

The leap to founder

Think IT Ai, Tampa Bay

I left the distributor side to become the partner. As CEO and Founder of Think IT Ai, I ran the whole business: sales, delivery, and full profit and loss ownership.

  • Founded and scaled a 10 person managed services company
  • Sold into government and education accounts through multi party pursuits
  • Sold the company in 2019
  • Told the full story on the Channel Journeys CJ9 podcast
Act Three

The operator

President, AC4S Technologies

Today I run AC4S Technologies, a technology, managed services, and cybersecurity company, as its President and platform owner on a Microsoft and ConnectWise stack.

  • Grew company valuation from $3.9M to $6.6M in under two years
  • Owns partner development and strategic relationships across vendors, distributors, telecom providers, and advisory partners
  • Leads joint business planning, QBRs, roadmaps, and renewals
  • Delivery leadership, including a Genetec access control program and a campus video wall and camera program

Mentoring

Five years a Big Brother.

Gary spent five years as a Big Brother with Big Brothers Big Sisters, showing up for one kid, week after week, year after year. It is the same commitment he makes to partners and teams, just measured in a young person's life instead of a quota.

He also gives time to student STEM programs, including judging STEM projects at Northglenn High School in April 2023. The rockets are real: build them together, then go outside and launch them.
